verdict: Datadog grew revenue 36% to $1.12B as big customers expanded their usage, but stock pay ate almost all of the operating profit — GAAP operating income was just $5M, with net income of $45M helped by interest earnings.

segments.name: Platform subscriptions
segments.note: One integrated platform — monitoring, security and AI observability, priced per host and per feature. Datadog reports a single revenue stream.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the platform and its AI features — by far the biggest running cost.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling to engineering and security teams at large companies.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

takeaways.title: Growth stayed hot
takeaways.text: Revenue grew 36% to $1.12B, and customers spending $100k+ a year rose 23% to about 4,720 — big companies keep putting more of their systems on Datadog.

takeaways.title: Stock pay is the whole gap
takeaways.text: GAAP operating income was just $5M, while non-GAAP operating income was $257M. Almost the entire difference is $220M of stock-based compensation — pay delivered in shares rather than cash.

takeaways.title: Cash flow tells a richer story
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $279M — 25 cents per revenue dollar — and Datadog held $5.0B of cash and marketable securities at quarter-end.

oneTimers: Stock-based compensation was $220M in the quarter, and G&A included $2M of M&A transaction costs (Datadog acquired AI startup Adaptive ML in the quarter).
otherDetail: Other income of $46M, net — $50M of interest income and other income, minus $3M of interest expense on Datadog's convertible notes.
follow100Note: Rows add up with a small rounding difference.
